scenario: A 35-year-old man burned his hands on a stove and did not feel it. He still feels cotton on the same skin. The loss is over both shoulders and the hands. A classmate calls it a peripheral neuropathy because the hands are numb.
question: Which fibers were cut, and why is touch spared?
options: Dorsal columns, so pain should be the spared sense
Crossing pain fibers in a central cavity
A peripheral nerve, which spares touch and removes pain only
A complete cord cut, so all sensation below a level is gone
A cortical sensory stroke, so both hands lose touch and pain together
correctAnswer: Crossing pain fibers in a central cavity
citation: Dalley AF, Agur AMR. Moore's Clinically Oriented Anatomy. 9th ed. Wolters Kluwer; 2023.
examTakeaway: A central cord cavity hits crossing spinothalamic fibers first, so pain and temperature are lost in a cape over the shoulders while touch remains.
